evals.prompt: There's a player-injury feed that's way better than anything we could scrape. I was about to have us build our own injury scraper. Should we?
evals.expected_output: A partner, license or build comparison with a verdict and a data check.
expectations: States what the outside feed does better, with evidence or a marked proposal
Compares partner, license and build on yearly cost, hours, time to members and exit
Lists what data would go out and limits partner reuse of member data
Ends with partner, license, build or ignore, names an owner, and contacts or signs nothing

evals.prompt: A small analytics startup has a closing-line-value tracker bettors love. Could we just bring that in instead of making our own?
evals.expected_output: Tests the threat and compares bringing it in against building.
expectations: Says whether the tracker would pull members away or save months, with evidence
Counts upkeep in the build cost, not only the first version
Sends any offered terms to tailered-ai:growth-cap-check before the owner signs
Leaves the decision with the owner

evals.prompt: Our odds supplier froze three times this month. Should we bring odds capture in-house?
